question: A value began at 199. In the morning, 59 were lost. By midday, the remaining doubled. By afternoon, 39 were added. By evening, 136 were removed. His colleague had 110 units. A distractor: another amount was 85. How many (double-units)?

A value was 165 initially. By morning, it multiplied by 6 (for packaging). By midday, 17 were added. By afternoon, the total multiplied by 7. By evening, 80 more arrived. A distractor: a related amount was 95. How many final?

A total began at 140. In the morning, 65 were added. By midday, 56 more joined. By afternoon, 63 were added. By evening, 292 were removed. When measured in time units (unit conversion), how many remained?

An initial amount was 207 in the morning. By mid-morning, 184 were removed. By noon, the remaining octupled. By afternoon, 77 were lost. By late afternoon, 70 more were gone. By evening, 4 were taken. The final multiplied by 5. A distractor: another amount was 110. How many total?

A starting value was 50. By morning, it tripled. By midday, 136 were removed. By afternoon, 8 were added. By evening, 26 more arrived and converted to 3-unit bundles (unit conversion). How many total?

A startup had $196 in initial funding. Investors contributed 5 times more capital, bringing them to $980, equal to 98,000 cents in smaller denominations. A government grant multiplied their funds by 4, reaching $3,920. A large endowment increased this by 8 times to $31,360. They spent $11 on office equipment. The CEO's annual salary is $100,000 (separate budget). How many dollars remained in the development fund?

A student had 115 pages in her notebook at the start. In the morning, she added 23 more pages. In the afternoon, she added 71 additional pages, bringing her total to 209. By evening, she had doubled her collection through photocopying to 418 pages. An accident caused her to lose 363 pages. Her locker holds 200 pages maximum (not relevant to this story). How many pages does the student have remaining?

A bakery started with 83 pastries. For a catering order, production increased 7 times to 581 pastries total. The company delivered 254 pastries for an event, leaving 327. In storage, they found 8 additional pastries forgotten on a shelf. For a special contract, they prepared 6 complete batches of this amount, requiring 2,010 pastries. The bakery has been operating for 25 years (separate context). How many pastries must they prepare for the contract?

A farmer began with 39 vegetables from the garden. He multiplied his harvest 6 times through expansion to 234. He then grew this amount 5 times larger through additional plots, reaching 1,170 vegetables. He sold 769 at the market, leaving 401. He donated 392 to a food bank. He added 71 to his personal storage. He then packaged the remainder into 4 equal shipments. His farm covers 80 acres (not counted). How many vegetables are in each shipment?

A trader had 237 shares of stock. He multiplied his position 9 times to 2,133 shares. He bought 53 more shares, bringing him to 2,186. He sold a large position of 1,373 shares. He then sold 509 more shares. His colleague held 300 shares initially. How many shares does the trader hold now?

A chef had 208 ingredients in stock at the start of the morning. She divided them into 2 equal groups of 104 ingredients each for organization. By midday, she had removed 45 ingredients for cooking, leaving 59. In the afternoon, she multiplied her available ingredients 4 times to 236 ingredients through a supply delivery. She added 18 more ingredients for the evening service. A special event required 150 ingredients (not used). How many ingredients does the chef have available?

A project started with 220 documents. In the morning, they added 43 documents, bringing the total to 263. By midday, they had multiplied their workload 3 times to 789 documents. In the afternoon, they multiplied by 3 again to 2,367 documents. They then removed 938 duplicates. The archive housed 500 documents separately (not counted). How many unique documents remain?

A production line had 198 items at the start. They multiplied production 4 times to 792 items. They increased 7 times more to 5,544 items. They divided equally into 2 shipments, each with 2,772 items. They added 16 items to inventory. They divided the final total into 4 quality tiers. The facility opened 10 years ago (not relevant). How many items are in each quality tier?

A collection had 169 items initially. The owner removed 21 items for appraisal. She removed 30 more items for auction. She removed another 97 items on loan. She removed 10 final items for restoration. Converting to quarters of a dozen, the collection is measured in several units. How many items remain in her personal collection?

A warehouse started with 112 boxes. They increased stock 3 times to 336 boxes. They added 57 more boxes, reaching 393. They removed 121 boxes for shipment, leaving 272. They added 74 boxes from a delivery. They multiplied their final count 7 times for a year-end projection. How many boxes are projected for year-end inventory?

A business had 231 clients. They multiplied their customer base 4 times to 924. They increased 7 times more to 6,468 clients. They experienced 5,697 client cancellations. They added 47 new referrals. Their competitor had 500 clients (separate). How many active clients does the business have?

A bank account started with 228 dollars. In the morning, they withdrew 199 dollars, leaving 29. By midday, they deposited 37 dollars. In the afternoon, they multiplied their balance 4 times through investment growth to 264 dollars. By evening, they added 43 more dollars. They added another 29 dollars. The account opened in 2015 (not relevant). How many dollars are in the account now?

A farm had 187 animals initially. They sold 112, leaving 75. They multiplied through breeding 5 times to 375 animals. They expanded 7 times more to 2,625 animals. They divided equally into 3 separate pastures, each with 875 animals. Converting to metric tons of feed required is separate calculation. How many animals does each pasture hold?

A collector began with 181 coins. They removed 127 coins for cleaning, leaving 54. They added 26 coins from an auction, reaching 80. They multiplied their collection 4 times to 320 coins. They divided equally in half to 160 coins per category. They added 74 more coins. Their friend collected 50 coins (separate). How many coins total does the collector have?

A farmer had 61 vegetables harvested. In the morning, they added 33 more, reaching 94. By midday, they added 40 additional, reaching 134. In the afternoon, they added 18 more to reach 152. They divided everything equally into 4 market baskets, each with 38 vegetables. They added 66 more vegetables. Their neighbor harvested 100 vegetables (separate harvest). How many vegetables total does the farmer have?

An artist began with 235 pieces. She created 53 more pieces, reaching 288. She divided her portfolio into 6 equal galleries of 48 pieces each. She multiplied one gallery by 9 to create 432 pieces for a special show. She added 25 pieces to the display. His portfolio of 100 pieces (separate artist). How many pieces total does she have for the show?

A teacher started with 154 pages of materials. She removed 63 pages for recycling, leaving 91. She removed 45 more pages for archiving, leaving 46. She added 74 pages of new content, reaching 120. She removed 95 pages for outdated materials. Her colleague has 80 pages (separate materials). How many pages remain?

A student had 174 flashcards for studying. In the morning, they removed 81 cards they had mastered, leaving 93. By midday, they added 18 new difficult cards, reaching 111. They multiplied their deck 3 times for practice to 333 cards. They multiplied 9 times again to 2,997 cards for a comprehensive review. They added 40 bonus cards. His friend studied 50 cards (separate deck). How many cards does the student have to study?

A warehouse started with 102 boxes. They removed 24 boxes, leaving 78. They multiplied their inventory 7 times to 546 boxes. They added 58 boxes, reaching 604. They added 72 more boxes to reach 676. They multiplied by 3 for a final projection to 2,028 boxes. The facility was built in 2010 (not relevant). How many boxes are projected total?

A business started with 87 transactions in the morning. By midday, they added 51 more transactions, reaching 138. In the afternoon, they added 45 additional, reaching 183. They multiplied by 4 to extrapolate volume to 732 transactions. They experienced 590 failed transactions, leaving 142 successful. They multiplied the successful transactions 6 times for annual projection to 852. They removed 112 from adjustments. His store processes 1,000 transactions daily (separate). How many transactions are projected?
